ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r5.claim: Most read قنطوا with fatḥ; al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb read it with kasr.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r6.claim: God's spreading mercy includes the benefits and fertility brought by rain, though it is broader than rain; al-Suddī identifies mercy with rain, while al-Mahdawī says it can be sunshine after prolonged rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r6.anchor: يظهرها من آثار الغيث من المنافع والخصب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r7.claim: God is the protector of His servants and is praised for the favors He bestows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p337/r7.anchor: وهو الولي: الذي يتولى عباده، الحميد: المحمود على ما أسدى من نعمائه

STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.claim: God is Provider and Sustainer, owns the keys of heaven and earth, and distributes provision by wisdom; this applies to wealth, offspring, and revelation.
STUDYQURAN:42:intro/r11.anchor: the Provider and Sustainer unto Whom belong the keys of the heavens and the earth (v. 12) and Who provides as He wills in accord with His Wisdom

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r2.claim: God sends rain when people despair; because livelihood depends on it, this reminds them that neither deities nor human means control their provision.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r2.anchor: sending down rain from the blocked crevices of the sky is only in the hands of the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r3.claim: Rain is an everyday sign that God alone is the true accomplisher and al-Ḥamīd, worthy of good attributes, praise, and gratitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p144/r3.anchor: this every day observation shows that the real accomplisher is God and He is

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p145/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p145/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p145/r1.claim: God continues to sustain people through worldly life even when they challenge Him despite living on His provision.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p145/r1.anchor: people who thrive on his sustenance and even challenge Him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r1.claim: The listed blessings are signs of God's oneness and show that He alone deserves worship, without rivals.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r1.anchor: هذه تعديد نعمة الله تعالى الدالة على وحدانيته، وأنه الإله الذي يستحق أن يعبد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r2.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce yunazzilu with a doubled zāy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r3.speaker: ابن وثاب والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r3.claim: Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read yunazzilu with a lightened zāy; the reading is also reported from Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Ḥātim prefers it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r3.anchor: وقرأها «ينزل» مخففة ابن وثاب والأعمش، ورويت عن أبي عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim prefers the lightened reading of yunazzilu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r4.anchor: ورجحها أبو حاتم، وقرأ جمهور الناس: «قنطوا» بفتح النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r5.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r5.claim: Most readers pronounce qanatū with fatḥa on the nūn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r6.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash pronounce qanatū with kasra on the nūn; both vocalizations are Arabic variants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش: بكسر النون، وقد تقدم ذكرها وهما لغتان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r7.claim: When told the land was dry and people despaired, ʿUmar replied that they would receive rain, expressing relief's arrival in hardship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r7.anchor: أجدبت الأرض وقنط الناس، فقال: مطروا إذا، بمعنى أن الفرج عند الشدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r8.claim: One group says that “His mercy” means rain, so the second phrase repeats and reinforces the same blessing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r8.anchor: واختلف المتأولون في قوله تعالى: وينشر رحمته فقالت فرقة: أراد بالرحمة المطر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r9.claim: Another group says “His mercy” means the sun, a separate blessing: rain is welcome after drought but tiresome if prolonged, so sunshine becomes precious.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الرحمة في هذا الموضع الشمس، فذلك تعديد نعمة غير الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r10.claim: God is the protector whose acts and blessings benefit those He favors and deserve praise, unlike idols that neither harm nor benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p36#2/r10.anchor: فهو الذي ينفع إذا والى وتحمد أفعاله ونعمه، لا كالذي لا يضر ولا ينفع من أوثانكم

MUQATIL:42:27-32/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r2.claim: After Meccans despaired during a seven-year withholding of rain, God sent rain and spread His blessing; He is believers' protector and praised by creation for the rain.
MUQATIL:42:27-32/r2.anchor: المطر الذى حبس عنهم بمكة سبع سنين، { من بعد ما قنطوا } ، يعنى من بعد الإياسة

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r9.claim: After explaining why God does not give more than needed when excess would harm faith, Al-Razi adds that He provides when people need sustenance.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r9.anchor: ولما بين تعالى أنه لا يعطيهم ما زاد على قدر حاجتهم لأجل أنه علم أن تلك الزيادة تضرهم في دينهم

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r10.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r10.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Asim read ينزل with doubling; the other reciters read it lightly.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r10.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم { ينزل } مشددة والباقون مخففة

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r11.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r11.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf reports two readings of قنطوا, with the nun vowel opened or kasra.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r11.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرىء { قنطوا } بفتح النون وكسرها

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r12.claim: Rain after despair makes gratitude more likely because joy at a blessing received after hardship is fuller.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r12.anchor: وإنزال الغيث بعد القنوط أدعى إلى الشكر لأن الفرح بحصول النعمة بعد البلية أتم

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r13.claim: The mercy spread is the rain's blessings and benefits, including the fertility it produces.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r13.anchor: أي بركات الغيث ومنافعه وما يحصل به من الخصب

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r14.claim: Alternatively, mercy may mean the broad mercy present in everything: God sends the rain that is itself mercy and spreads other kinds of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد رحمته الواسعة في كل شيء كأنه قيل ينزل الرحمة التي هي الغيث

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r15.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r15.claim: When told that drought had become severe and people despaired, Umar replied, “Then they will be rained on,” intending this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r15.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قيل له ( اشتد القحط وقنط الناس فقال : إذن مطروا )

RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r16.claim: The wali is the one who manages His servants kindly; al-Hamid is praised for bringing creation its various forms of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p147/r16.anchor: الذي يتولى عباده بإحسانه و { العزيز الحميد } المحمود على ما يوصل للخلق من أقسام الرحمة

STUDYQURAN:42:28/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r1.claim: God sends rain when people have despaired, at their time of need, and spreads it over those in the region.
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r1.anchor: When people have given up hope that rain will fall, God sends it upon them at their time of need (cf. 30:49; 41:39)

STUDYQURAN:42:28/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r2.claim: Spiritually, divine inspirations revive dead hearts through remembrance and knowledge after despair.
STUDYQURAN:42:28/r2.anchor: Divine inspirations down upon dead hearts such that they are revived through remembrance [of God] and knowledge, after they have despaired” (Aj)

TAB-FULL:v20p511/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r1.claim: God sends rain from the sky to relieve people after they have despaired of its arrival; the mercy He spreads here is the rain itself.
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {من بعد ما قنطوا} [الشورى: 28] قال: «يئسوا»

TAB-FULL:v20p511/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses قنطوا as they despaired.
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {من بعد ما قنطوا} [الشورى: 28] قال: «يئسوا»

TAB-FULL:v20p511/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r3.claim: In two reports, Umar answers news that the land was barren and people despaired by saying they would be rained on, invoking the verse.
TAB-FULL:v20p511/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: أنه قيل لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: أجدبت الأرض، وقنط الناس قال: «مطروا إذن»

TAB-FULL:v20p512/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p512/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p512/r1.claim: God is the one who cares for people through His beneficence and grace, praised for His favors and blessings in creation.
TAB-FULL:v20p512/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وهو الولي الحميد} [الشورى: 28] يقول: وهو الذي يليكم بإحسانه وفضله، الحميد بأياديه عندكم

BURSEVI:v8p245/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245/r1.claim: Al-ghayth is rain that relieves people from drought, specifically beneficial rain, since rain can harm or come at the wrong time.
BURSEVI:v8p245/r1.anchor: {وهو الذى ينزل الغيث} ؛ أي : المطر الذي يغيث الناس من الجدب ، ولذلك خص بالنافع منه

BURSEVI:v8p245/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v8p245/r2.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes الغيث, used for rain, from الغوث, used for aid.
BURSEVI:v8p245/r2.anchor: قال الراغب : الغيث : يقال في المطر والغوث في النصرة.

BURSEVI:v8p245/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245/r3.claim: Mentioning rain after despair recalls the fullness of the blessing: relief after hopelessness and hardship brings greater joy and prompts gratitude, although rain also comes at other times.
BURSEVI:v8p245/r3.anchor: {منا بعد ما قنطوا} ؛ أي : يئسوا منه وتقييد تنزيله بذلك مع تحققه بدونه أيضا ، لتذكير كمال النعمة

BURSEVI:v8p245/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245/r4.claim: ينشر means to spread or scatter.

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r1.claim: The mercy spread is rain’s blessings and benefits throughout plains and mountains, plants and animals.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r1.anchor: بركات الغيث ومنافعه في كل شيء من السهل والجبل والنبات والحيوان.

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r2.speaker: فتح الرحمن
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r2.claim: Fath al-Rahman takes the mercy as sunshine, a separate blessing: rain delights after despair but becomes tiresome when prolonged, making sun welcome afterward.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r2.anchor: وفي "فتح الرحمن" : وينشر رحمته ، وهي الشمس

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r3.claim: Al-Wali is the master who cares for His servants through beneficence and the spreading of mercy.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r3.anchor: المالك السيد الذي يتولى عباده بالإحسان ونشر الرحمة.

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r4.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r4.claim: Al-Kashifi calls God the believers’ friend, who repairs their affairs by sending rain and spreading mercy and kindness.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r4.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (واوست دوست مؤمنان وسازنده كار ايشان بفرسنادن باران ونشر رحمت واحسان)

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r5.claim: Al-Hamid means the one who alone deserves praise for this and all other acts.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r5.anchor: المستحق للحمد على ذلك وغيره لا غيره.

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r6.claim: Another view makes al-Wali the controller who repeatedly sends rain, and al-Hamid the praiseworthy one: wise rain reveals need, strengthens resolve, and God answers the distressed.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وهو الولي ؛ أي : مولى المطر ومتصرفه يرسله مرة بعد مرة الحميد ؛ أي : الأهل

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r7.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r7.claim: During severe drought and public despair, Umar said that it must mean rain had come, alluding to this verse.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r7.anchor: وقيل لعمر رضي الله عنه اشتد القحط وقنط الناس ، فقال : مطروا إذن وأراد هذه الآية.

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r8.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r8.claim: The Mathnawi depicts calamity as prompting supplication and intercession, followed by God’s address that He has given them drink.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r8.anchor:
وفي المثنوي :
تافرود آيد بلاى دافعى
جون نباشداذ تضرع شافعى

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a sea beneath the Throne supplying animal provisions by divine command; rain descends heaven to heaven, is strained, and each measured drop is placed by an angel, except the unmeasured Flood.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أن تحت العرش بحرا ينزل منه أرزاق الحيوانات

BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r10.claim: Reports say angels know the annual rain amount and that years do not differ in total; a hadith says sins shift rain to others, or, if all sin, to deserts and seas.
BURSEVI:v8p245#2/r10.anchor: وروي : أن الملائكة يعرفون عدد المطر ومقداره في كل عام ؛ لأنه لا يختلف فيه البلاد ، وفي الحديث : "ما من سنة بأمطر من أخرى

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r4.claim: Qanūṭ means despair, and ghayth means rain.

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r5.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r5.claim: Majmaʿ al-Bayān distinguishes ghayth as rain beneficial in its season, while maṭar can be beneficial or harmful, in or out of season.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r5.anchor: قال في مجمع البيان الغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r6.claim: Spreading mercy means distributing blessings through the growth of plants and production of fruit caused by rain.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r6.anchor: ونشر الرحمة تفريق النعمة بين الناس بإنبات النبات وإخراج الثمار التي يكون سببها المطر

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r7.claim: The discussion shifts from provision to signs of divine unity connected with provision, and further signs follow.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r7.anchor: وفي الآية انتقال من حديث الرزق إلى آيات التوحيد

TABATABAI:42:28-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r8.claim: The closing names al-Walī and al-Ḥamīd praise God for His beautiful action.
TABATABAI:42:28-29/r8.anchor: وتذييل الآية بالاسمين الولي الحميد وهما من أسمائه تعالى الحسنى للثناء عليه في فعله الجميل

TABRISI:42:27-30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r2.claim: Ghayth is rain that is beneficial at its proper time; matar can be beneficial or harmful, in or out of season.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r2.anchor: والغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته والمطر قد يكون نافعا وقد يكون ضارا في وقته وغير وقته

TABRISI:42:27-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r3.claim: Rain after people despair of its coming more strongly elicits gratitude and recognition of the giver's kindness.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r3.anchor: ووجه إنزاله بعد القنوط أنه ادعى إلى شكر الآتي به وتعظيمه والمعرفة بموقع إحسانه

TABRISI:42:27-30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r4.claim: Spreading mercy means distributing blessings and bringing forth the plants and fruits caused by rain.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r4.anchor: أي ويفرق نعمته ويبسطها بإخراج النبات والثمار التي يكون سببها المطر

TABRISI:42:27-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r5.claim: God is the guardian who manages His servants, their affairs and interests, and owns them.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r5.anchor: الذي يتولى تدبير عباده وتقدير أمورهم ومصالحهم المالك لهم

TABRISI:42:27-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:42:27-30/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:42:27-30/r6.claim: God is praised for all His acts because all of them are kindness and benefit.
TABRISI:42:27-30/r6.anchor: المحمود على جميع أفعاله لكون جميعها إحسانا ومنافع

THALABI:v8p318/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p318/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p318/r2.claim: Ghayth means rain; the word comes from its helping people and putting their condition right.
THALABI:v8p318/r2.anchor: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث يعني المطر، سمي بذلك لأنه يغيث الناس أي يجيرهم ويصلح حالهم.

THALABI:v8p318/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p318/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
THALABI:v8p318/r3.claim: Al-Asmai relates that, after rain, an Arab woman described the rainfall by saying, We received as much rain as we wished.
THALABI:v8p318/r3.anchor: قال الأصمعي: مررت ببعض قبائل العرب وقد مطروا، فسألت عجوز منهم، كم أتاكم المطر؟ فقالت: غثنا ما شئنا.

THALABI:v8p318/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p318/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p318/r4.claim: Spreading God's mercy here means spreading rain, as in the verse about sending winds before His mercy.
THALABI:v8p318/r4.anchor: من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته ويبسط مطره نظيره قوله: وهو الذي يرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته

THALABI:v8p318/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p318/r5.speaker: قتادة عن سعيد
THALABI:v8p318/r5.claim: Qatada reports that during a drought, when people despaired, a man told Umar about it; Umar answered, You have been rained upon, and recited this verse.
THALABI:v8p318/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن رجلا أتى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه، فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين قحط المطر وقنط الناس. قال: مطرتم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:28/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:28/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:28/r1.claim: God sends rain after people despair of its coming and spreads His mercy by extending the rain.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:42:28/r1.anchor: المطر { من بعد ما قنطوا } من بعد يأس العباد من نزوله

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:28/r1.claim: God sends rain after people have lost hope, spreads His mercy, and is the true protector and worthy of all praise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:42:28/r1.anchor: İnsanlar bütün ümitlerini yitirdikten sonra yağmuru indiren ve rahmetini yayan O’dur. Gerçek dost ve koruyucu, her türlü hamde lâyık olan O’dur.

QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r6.claim: Outwardly, when people despair of rain and the land is drought-stricken, God sends rain near the point when hope is lost and revives the earth with mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r6.anchor: بعدما أصاب الأرض جدوبة ، وأبطأ نزول الغيث ، وقنط الناس من مجيء المطر ، وأشرف الوقت على حد الفوات

QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r7.claim: God also revives hearts: when the branch of one’s spiritual time withers, love clouds over, intimacy dims, and nearness recedes, divine mercy may rain upon the innermost self and renew intimacy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r7.anchor: فلربما ينظر إليه الحق برحمته ؛ فينزل على سره أمطار الرحمة ، ويعود عوده طريا

QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r8.claim: The poem hopes that estrangement will end, old covenants will live again, and a withered branch will turn green and sway.
QUSHAYRI:v3p166/r8.anchor: ولعل عهدك باللوى . . . يحيا فقد تحيا العهود والغصن ييبس تارة . . . وتراه مخضرا يميد

BURHAN:v3p444/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p444/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p444/r10.claim: One reading takes al-Walī and al-Ḥamīd as divine names: God cares for servants through mercy, and is either a praiser of obedient servants or praised in ease and hardship. Alternatively both refer to rain, the spring rain being walī and praiseworthy.
BURHAN:v3p444/r10.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الولي من أسماء المطر وهو مطر الربيع والحميد بمعنى المحمود وعلى هذا فالضمير عائد على الغيث

SULAMI:v2p228#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says God moves servants between hope and despair: when they hope, He exposes their limitations; when they despair, He gives hope through His attributes, and comforts those who fear despair.
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إن الله عز وجل يربى عباده بين طمع ويأس فإذا طمعوا فيه آيسهم بصفاتهم وإذا أيسوا أطمعهم بصفاته

SULAMI:v2p228#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r2.claim: He interprets the rain as mercy descending on the hearts of saints and establishing repentance, return, watchfulness, and care.
SULAMI:v2p228#3/r2.anchor: معنى ينزل الغيث رحمته على قلوب أوليائه فيثبت فيها التوبة والإنابة والمراقبة والرعاية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r1.claim: The claim that the finest poetry is truthful may mean poetry offering sound wisdom, moral counsel, and distinctions between good and bad conduct.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r1.anchor: خير الشعر ما دل على حكمة يقبلها العقل وأدب يجب به الفضل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r2.claim: Truthful praise can mean praising men only for qualities they actually possess, as the source says Zuhayr did.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r2.anchor: كما قيل كان زهير لا يمدح الرجل إلا بما فيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r3.claim: The opposing view calls the best poetry the most untrue: poetic craft expands through imaginative claims, figurative extension, and exaggeration in praise, blame, and description.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r3.anchor: ومن قال اكذبه ذهب إلى أن الصنعة إنما يمد باعها وينشر شعاعها ويتسع ميدانها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r4.claim: The author prefers truthful poetry: its sound reasoning, durable effect, clearer benefit, and richer yield outweigh the wider invention available to imaginative poetry.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r4.anchor: والأول أولى لأنهما قولان يتعارضان في اختيار نوعى الشعر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r5.claim: Reason and verification ultimately support the truthful kind of poetry, even though imaginative poetry offers a wider field for invention.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p236/r5.anchor: والعقل بعد على تفضيل القبيل الأول وتقديمه وتفخيم قدره وتعظيمه

DAMGHANI:v1p198/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r7.claim: Raḥma can mean rain; Dāmghānī groups this verse with several passages describing God's rain.
DAMGHANI:v1p198/r7.anchor: " وينشر رحمته " يعني المطر كقوله تعالى في سورة الروم " فانظر إلى آثار رحمة الله "

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r10.claim: Some add a seventeenth sense: raḥma means the sun, as in 42:28.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r10.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها سابع عشر فقال : الرحمة : الشمس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r1.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r1.claim: Ibn Fāris says rajāʾ with long ā means hope; short rajā is the edge of a well or any side, plural arjāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن فارس اللغوي : الرجاء بالمد . الأمل .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r2.claim: Hope can stand for fear; some speakers use mā arjū to mean they do not care, as in a line about a bee sting.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r2.anchor: وربما عبر عن الخوف بالرجاء وناس من أهل اللغة يقولون ما أرجو ، أي : ما أبالي وأنشدوا : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r3.claim: The common Qurʾanic sense of rajāʾ is hope, as in those who hope for God’s mercy.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير بأن الرجاء في القرآن على وجهين : - أحدهما : الأمل . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ أولئك يرجون رحمة الله ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r4.claim: A second Qurʾanic sense is fear, including fear of meeting God, the Last Day, and the reckoning.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p307#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : الخوف . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس : ﴿ إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ﴾

SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r1.claim: ما is a verbal noun: من بعد ما قنطوا means after their despair.
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r1.anchor: قوله: { من بعد ما قنطوا }: " ما " مصدرية أي: من قنوطهم.

SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r2.claim: The common reading opens the nūn; Yahya ibn Waththab and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, a dialectal form. The canonical form in 39:53 is also open; a kasra in the past is rare.
SAMIN-DURR:42:28/r2.anchor: والعامة على فتح النون. وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش بكسرها وهي لغة،

ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r3.claim: Qaniṭū is also read with kasra on the nūn; both qaniṭa yaqniṭu and qanaṭa yaqnaṭu mean to despair.
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r3.anchor: ويقرأ (قنطوا) بكسر النون، يقال قنط يقنط

ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r4.speaker: عمر
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r4.claim: When Umar was told the land had become barren and people had despaired, he replied that rain would come, invoking this verse.
ZAJJAJ:v4p399/r4.anchor: ويروى أن عمر قيل له قد أجدبت الأرض وقنط الناس فقال: مطروا إذن، لهذه الآية

ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r1.claim: The life-giving rain image connects to the preceding statement that God bestows grace in due measure.
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r1.anchor: This reference to the symbol of life-giving rain connects with the preceding statement

ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r2.claim: The rain reference prepares for the next verse's account of creation as a sign of God's existence and purposeful activity, and of life's continuation in the hereafter.
ASAD-NOTES:42:28#n32/r2.anchor: the statement in the next verse that all creation is but a visible "sign" or "revelation" of God's existence

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f2.claim: The Quran uses amṭara for punitive rain but ghayth for good: 42:28 brings mercy after despair, and 12:49 describes a year of relief and harvest.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r2#2/f2.anchor: لا تجد القرآن يلفظ به إلا في موضع الانتقام بخلاف الغيث الذي يذكره القرآن في الخير

NASHR:v2p218/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p218/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p218/r10.claim: In the general imperfect class with prefixed tāʾ/yāʾ/nūn and initial ḍamma, Ibn Kathir and the Basrans lighten; Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf join them for ينزل الغيث in al-Shura and Luqman. The source notes several surah-specific exceptions.
NASHR:v2p218/r10.anchor: ينزل وبابه إذا كان فعلا مضارعا، أوله تاء، أو ياء

QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#1/r1.claim: The standard Form II with shadda marks repeated, intensified, or staged causative descent of rain.
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#1/r1.anchor: Canonical standard line vocalizes Form II with shadda, marking repeated, intensified, or staged causative descent

QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#2/r1.claim: Form IV without shadda presents the rain’s descent as caused sending-down with less overt staging force.
QIRAAT-ER:42:28:4#2/r1.anchor: Canonical variant reads Form IV without shadda, presenting the rain's descent as caused sending-down

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p191#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p191#5/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p191#5/r1.claim: When told that drought had left the land barren and people despairing, ʿUmar replied that they would then receive rain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p191#5/r1.anchor: قيل لعمر بن الخطاب أجدبت الأرض وقنط الناس قال مطروا إذا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r1.claim: Ghayth is rain that brings relief from drought and is beneficial; not every kind of rain is called ghayth.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r1.anchor: أيالمطرالذي يغيثهممن الجدب ولذلك خصبالنافع منه فلا يقال غيث لكل مطر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r2.claim: The majority read yunazzilu with a light consonant, without doubling.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r3.claim: Mentioning that the rain comes after people despair of it recalls God's favor, though the rain also descends at other times.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r3.anchor: وتقييد تنزيلهبذلك معتحققه بدونهأيض التذكير النعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r4.speaker: الأعمش وابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththab read qanitu with kasra on the nūn.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r5.claim: God spreads the rain's benefits and effects through plains, mountains, plants, and animals; alternatively, this refers broadly to His encompassing mercy, of which those are a primary instance.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r5.anchor: أي منافع الغيثوآثاره في كلشيء من السهل والجبل والنبات والحيوان أو رحمته الواسعة المنتظمة لما ذكر انتظاماأوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r6.speaker: المهدوي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the mercy is the sun appearing after prolonged rain has wearied people; the author rejects this as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r6.anchor: وقيل : الرحمة هناظهورالشمس لأنهإذادام المطرسئمفتجيء الشمس بعده عظيمة الموقع ذكره المهدوي وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r7.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r7.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the mercy as the rain itself, which the author calls very far-fetched because it repeats the same blessing in two expressions.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r7.anchor: ومنالبعيد جداما قاله السدي من أن الرحمة هنا الغيث نفسه عدد النعمة نفسها بلفظين

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r8.claim: The pronoun in His mercy refers to God; under the first interpretation of mercy's spread, it may instead refer to the rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r8.anchor: فضمير ) رحمته للهعز وجل وجوز على الأول كونه للغيث

ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r9.claim: Al-Wali is the one who benevolently tends His servants and spreads mercy; al-Hamid is the one alone deserving praise for this.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p39/r9.anchor: وهو الولي ( الذييتولى عباده بالأحسان ونشرالرحمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r1.claim: Al-ghayth is rain, which God sends after people have despaired of it; this should increase their gratitude.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r1.anchor: المطر، {من بعد ما قنطوا} يعني: من بعد ما يئس الناس منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r2.claim: Muqātil says God withheld rain from the people of Mecca for seven years until they despaired, then sent it and reminded them of His favor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: حبس الله المطر عن أهل مكة سبع سنين حتى قنطوا، ثم أنزل الله المطر فذكرهم الله نعمته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r3.claim: The spreading of God's mercy means His spreading the rain, as also stated in Q 7:57.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p195#2/r4.claim: God is the patron of those who obey Him and is praised among His creatures.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r1.claim: Al-ghayth is rain that rescues people from drought, so the word is reserved for beneficial rain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r1.anchor: المطر الذي يغيثهم من الجدب ولذلك خص بالنافع

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r2.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and ʿAsim read the verb with a doubled zāy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم «ينزل» بالتشديد

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r3.claim: Qaniṭū means that they despaired of rain; a reading pronounces the nūn with kasra.

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r4.claim: God spreads His mercy through plains, mountains, plants, and animals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r4.anchor: في كل شيء من السهل والجبل والنبات والحيوان

BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:42:28-29/r5.claim: He is the guardian who cares for His servants graciously and spreads mercy, and is therefore deserving of praise.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r2.claim: God alone sends rain by choice; this counters those who attribute rainfall, vegetation, and crops to a habitual process of time.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r2.anchor: بين أنه سبحانه هو الفاعل لذلك بقدرته واختياره

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r3.claim: The verse uses the pronoun of the unseen because sending rain is one of the keys of the unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r3.anchor: معبرا بالضمير الذي هو غيب لأجل أن إنزال الغيث من مفاتيح الغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r4.claim: Al-ghayth is rain that brings succor: people receive what they asked for and are relieved outwardly, just as revelation relieves them outwardly and inwardly.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r5.claim: Rain comes after people have despaired of it and realized that no one else can send it, making them more inclined to give thanks.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r5.anchor: يئسوا من إنزاله وعملوا انه لا يقدر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r6.claim: Calling the rain mercy broadens its effects: it spreads over plains and mountains and produces pools, rivers, vegetation, trees, grain, fruit, and other benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r6.anchor: على السهل والجبل فينزل من السحاب المحمول بالريح من الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r7.claim: The softness of plants brought from hard soil and delicate branches from rough trees show God's power; denying resurrection or evading it is therefore foolish.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r7.anchor: فما أجلف من ينكر إخراجه الموتى من القبور

BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r8.claim: After rejecting the taking of patrons besides God and affirming that He alone is the Patron (42:9), the author points to rain and its effects as evidence of His care.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p629/r8.anchor: أنكر عليهم فيما مضى اتخاذ ولي من دونه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p630/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p630/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p630/r1.claim: Al-Walī is the one closest to His servants in every matter; al-Ḥamīd deserves every kind of praise and rewards obedience with increasing bounty and enduring closeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p630/r1.anchor: الذي لا أحد أقرب منه إلى عباده في شيء من الأشياء

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r8.claim: During a drought, a man told ʿUmar that rain had failed and people despaired; ʿUmar replied that they had been given rain and recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال لعمر رضي الله عنه: يا أمير المؤمنين قحط المطر وقنط الناس

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r9.claim: Mujāhid explains “after they despaired” as “after they had given up hope.”
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {من بعد ما قنطوا} قال: يئسوا

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r10.speaker: ثابت
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r10.claim: Thābit says they had heard that supplication is answered when rain falls, and cites this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r10.anchor: عن ثابت رضي الله عنه قال: بلغنا أنه يستجاب الدعاء عند المطر ثم تلا هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v7p353/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r11.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r11.claim: The Prophet says two supplications are not rejected: one made at the call to prayer and one made beneath the rain.
DURR-FULL:v7p353/r11.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ثنتان ما تردان: الدعاء عند النداء وتحت المطر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.claim: Muqatil excludes the passage from verse 23 through verse 24 from the otherwise Meccan surah; it is said to have been revealed about the Ansar and is among Ibn Abbas's four cited verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r1.anchor: وعن مقاتل استثناء قوله تعالى : { ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا إلى قوله : إنه عليم بذات الصدور }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.claim: Muqatil also says the passage in verses 39–41 about responding to aggression was revealed in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r3.anchor: وفيه عنه أن قوله تعالى : { والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون إلى قوله : ما عليهم من سبيل }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.speaker: الجعبري عن جابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.claim: In the order attributed by al-Jaʿbari from Jabir ibn Zayd, the surah followed al-Kahf and preceded Ibrahim, and was the sixty-ninth revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r4.anchor: وعدت التاسعة والستين في ترتيب نزول السور عند الجعبري المروي عن جابر بن زيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r5.claim: Muqatil says verse 28 was revealed when rain stopped in Mecca; if so, the surah's revelation began around year eight and may have continued into year nine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r5.anchor: إذا صح أن آية { وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا } ( الشورى : 28 ) نزلت في انحباس المطر عن أهل مكة كما قال مقاتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAshur suggests revelation may have continued into year nine, after the Aqaba pledge, because the Ansar could be intended in verse 38 even before the Hijra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r6.anchor: ولعل نزولها استمر إلى سنة تسع بعد أن آمن نقباء الأنصار ليلة العقبة فقد قيل : إن قوله : { والذين استجابوا لربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.claim: Madinan, Meccan, Syrian, and Basran verse counts give the surah fifty verses, while the Kufan count gives fifty-three.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r7.anchor: وعدت آيها عند أهل المدينة ومكة والشام والبصرة خمسين ، وعند أهل الكوفة ثلاثا وخمسين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.claim: The surah challenges those who deny revelation to produce speech like the Quran, a challenge common to surahs opened by disjointed letters, as in al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r8.anchor: أول أغراضها الإشارة إلى تحدي الطاعنين في أن القرآن وحي من الله بأن يأتوا بكلام مثله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.claim: God argues that Muhammad's revelation resembles that given to earlier messengers and warns Mecca and its surroundings of Judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r9.anchor: واستدل الله على المعاندين بأن الوحي إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما هو إلا كالوحي إلى الرسل من قبله لينذر أهل مكة ومن حولها بيوم الحساب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.claim: God owns the heavens and earth, whose realms submit to Him; as creator of beings, He chooses messengers and may legislate for this community as for earlier ones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r10.anchor: وأن الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض لا تعارض قدرته ولا يشك في حكمته ، وقد خضعت له العوالم العليا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.claim: All messengers sent to address people generally were human recipients of revelation; God had not previously sent angels to address the masses directly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r11.anchor: وما أرسل الله الرسل إلا من البشر يوحي إليهم فلم يسبق أن أرسل ملائكة لمخاطبة عموم الناس مباشرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.claim: The polytheists have no proof beyond imitating leaders of disbelief who instituted idolatry and planted doubts among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r12.anchor: وأن المشركين بالله لا حجة لهم إلا تقليد أيمة الكفر الذين شرعوا لهم الإشراك وألقوا إليهم الشبهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.claim: The surah warns of Judgment and the approaching Hour, describing idolaters' punishment while alluding to believers' honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r13.anchor: وحذرهم يوم الجزاء واقتراب الساعة وما سيلقى المشركون يوم الحساب من العذاب مع إدماج التعريض بالترغيب فيما سيلقاه المؤمنون من الكرامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.claim: Reflection shows that the Prophet does not invent claims about God, since God would not allow him to attribute words falsely to Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r14.anchor: وأنهم لو تدبروا لعلموا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يأتي عن الله من تلقاء نفسه لأن الله لا يقره على أن يقول عليه ما لم يقله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.claim: The surah presents signs of divine unity, including blessings such as navigation at sea and worldly provisions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p23#4/r15.anchor: وذكرت دلائل الوحدانية وما هو من تلك الآيات نعمة على الناس مثل دليل السير في البحر وما أوتيه الناس من نعم الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r9.claim: The rain verse is joined to measured provision because rain is a major source of sustenance and is itself sent in the measure God knows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r9.anchor: عطف على جملة { ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء } ( الشورى : 27 ) فإن الغيث سبب رزق عظيم وهو ما ينزله الله بقدر هو أعلم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r10.claim: Rain is singled out as a universally acknowledged blessing, foundational to life because it produces good food for people and animals; this prepares for the following sign of living creatures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p93/r10.anchor: وخصها بالذكر دون غيرها من النعم الدنيوية لأنها نعمة لا يختلف الناس فيها لأنها أصل دوام الحياة بإيجاد الغذاء الصالح للناس والدواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r1.claim: The imperfect verb indicates repeated and renewed sending of rain; the past tense in after they despaired shows their despair had occurred and endured for some time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r1.anchor: واختيار المضارع في { ينزل } لإفادة تكرر التنزيل وتجديده . والتعبير بالماضي في قوله : { من بعد ما قنطوا } للإشارة إلى حصول القنوط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r2.claim: Ghayth is rain that comes after drought; its name derives from the relief it brings to people in distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r2.anchor: والغيث : المطر الآتي بعد الجفاف ، سمي غيثا بالمصدر لأن به غيث الناس المضطرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r3.anchor: والقنوط : اليأس ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { فلا تكن من القانطين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r4.claim: They despaired of rain when the usual signs of rain disappeared and the planting season was running out.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r4.anchor: والمراد : من بعدما قنطوا من الغيث بانقطاع إمارات الغيث المعتادة وضيق الوقت عن الزرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r5.claim: The restrictive construction is a reversal of the assumption that rain is governed by stars: it directly counters polytheists and treats inattentive Muslims as if they relied on customary causes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r5.anchor: وصيغة القصر في قوله : { وهو الذي ينزل الغيث } تفيد قصر القلب لأن في السامعين مشركين يظنون نزول الغيث من تصرف الكواكب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r6.speaker: زيد بن خالد الجهني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r6.claim: After a night rain, the Prophet said people were divided: attributing rain to God's grace is faith in God and disbelief in stars, while attributing it to a star's phase reverses that allegiance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r6.anchor: وفي حديث زيد بن خالد الجهني قال : ( خطبنا رسول الله على إثر سماء كانت من الليل فقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r7.claim: Nashr is the opposite of folding and is used metaphorically here for expansion and extension.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r7.anchor: والنشر : ضد الطي ، وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { يلقاه منشورا } في سورة الإسراء . واستعير هنا للتوسيع والامتداد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r8.claim: Mercy here means God's mercy through water.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r9.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes the mercy to mean sunlight after the rain.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r10.claim: The pronoun in after they despaired refers to God's servants mentioned in verse 25.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r10.anchor: وضمير { من بعد ما قنطوا } عائد إلى { عباده من قوله : وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r11.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r11.claim: One account says the verse followed the lifting of a seven-year drought in Mecca through the Prophet's prayer; Quraysh had eaten carrion and bones, and the episode is alluded to in 44:15.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p95/r11.anchor: وقد قيل : إن الآية نزلت بسبب رفع القحط عن قريش بدعوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بهم بذلك بعد أن دام عليهم القحط سبع سنين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r1.claim: Al-Ṣaḥīḥ reports through Ibn Masud that after Quraysh rejected him, the Prophet prayed for seven years like Joseph; Abu Sufyan then pleaded for relief, and the Prophet prayed, warning they would relapse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r1.anchor: في ( الصحيح ) عن عبد الله بن مسعود ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دعا قريشا كذبوه واستعصوا عليه فقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r2.claim: The author says the event occurred in Medina and cites a report that the verse was revealed when a Bedouin asked the Prophet for rain during the Friday sermon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r2.anchor: وقد كان هذا في المدينة ويؤيده ما روي أن هذه الآية نزلت في استسقاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما سأله الأعرابي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r3.speaker: كعب بن مرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r3.claim: One version identifies the person who addressed the Prophet during the rain appeal as Kaʿb ibn Murra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r3.anchor: وفي رواية أن الذي كلمه هو كعب بن مرة وفي بعض الروايات في ( الصحيح ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r4.claim: Another version in al-Ṣaḥīḥ has the Prophet pray against Quraysh and ask that they endure years like Joseph's years.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات في ( الصحيح ) أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اللهم عليك بقريش اللهم اشدد وطأتك على مضر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r5.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r5.claim: These readers pronounce ينزل with fatḥa on the nūn and a doubled zāy; the remaining readers have sukūn on the nūn and a light zāy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r5.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو جعفر { ينزل } بفتح النون وتشديد الزاي .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r6.claim: The paired attributes suit deliverance: the protecting ally does good to those under his care, and the praiseworthy giver grants what merits praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r6.anchor: لمناسبتهما للإغاثة لأن الولي يحسن إلى مواليه والحميد يعطي ما يحمد عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r7.claim: Ḥamīd has the intensive adjective form faʿīl with passive meaning, mafʿūl.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r8.speaker: المهدوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawī explains the spreading of mercy as the sun appearing after rain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r8.anchor: وذكر المهدوي تفسير { ينشر رحمته } بطلوع الشمس بعد المطر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r9.claim: Rain is both a blessing and a sign of God's wondrous making and power, so the discourse digresses to signs affirming that God alone is divine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p96/r9.anchor: لما كان إنزال الغيث جامعا بين كونه نعمة وكونه آية دالة على بديع صنع الله تعالى وعظيم قدرته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r1.claim: A Qur’an commentator should learn the recurring conventions of Qur’anic wording and arrangement; some early authorities identified such patterns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r1.anchor: يحق على المفسر أن يتعرف عادات القرآن من نظمه وكلمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says every Qur’anic occurrence of “ka’s” means wine; al-Tabari also transmits this convention from al-Dahhak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : كل كاس في القرآن فالمراد بها الخمر . وذكر ذلك الطبري عن الضحاك أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r3.speaker: ابن عيينة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says the Qur’an uses “rain” (maṭar) only for punishment, while Arabs call rain “ghayth,” as in this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري في تفسير سورة الأنفال قال ابن عيينة : ما سمى الله مطرا في القرآن إلا عذابا ، وتسميه العرب الغيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Qur’anic addresses beginning “O people” refer to the Meccan polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن كل ما جاء من يا أيها الناس فالمقصود به أهل مكة المشركون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r5.speaker: الجاحظ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r5.claim: Al-Jahiz notes recurring paired concepts in the Qur’an: prayer and almsgiving, hunger and fear, paradise and hell, hope and dread, emigrants and helpers, and jinn and humans.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r5.anchor: وقال الجاحظ في البيان وفي القرآن معان لا تكاد تفترق ، مثل الصلاة والزكاة ، والجوع والخوف ، والجنة والنار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p124/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur adds benefit and harm, and heaven and earth, to al-Jahiz’s examples of paired Qur’anic concepts.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r1.claim: Ghayth means rain that comes when it is needed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r2.claim: Rain after despair is more likely to prompt gratitude to the one who sends it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r2.anchor: وذلك أدعى لهم إلى شكر منزله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r3.claim: Muqatil identifies the mercy spread as rain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r4.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r4.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi reports another view: the mercy is sunlight after the rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r4.anchor: والثاني الشمس بعد المطر حكاه أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r5.claim: He refers readers to his explanations of al-Wali at 4:45 and al-Hamid at 2:267.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p288/r5.anchor: وقد ذكرنا الولي في سورة النساء 45 والحميد في البقرة 267

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r1.claim: God sends rain after people have despaired of it, at the time they need it most; Ibn Kathir links this to the description of people’s despair before rain in 30:49.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r1.anchor: من بعد إياس الناس من نزول المطر، ينزله عليهم في وقت حاجتهم وفقرهم إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r2.claim: God spreads His mercy throughout the region and among its inhabitants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r2.anchor: يعم بها الوجود على أهل ذلك القطر وتلك الناحية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r3.claim: Qatadah reports that during a drought, when a man told Umar that rain had failed and people despaired, Umar replied that they had been given rain and recited this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب: يا أمير المؤمنين، قحط المطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.claim: God directs creation toward what benefits them in this life and the next, and the outcome of all He decrees and does is praiseworthy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p206#2/r4.anchor: هو المتصرف لخلقه بما ينفعهم في دنياهم وأخراهم، وهو المحمود العاقبة

JISHUMI:v9p6246/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r13.claim: Qunūṭ means despair; qanita has two reported vowel patterns in both the past and present forms.
JISHUMI:v9p6246/r13.anchor: والقنوط: اليأس، قنط يقنط بفتح النون وكسرها في الماضي والمضارع

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r1.claim: Nashr is the opposite of folding, and nashran can describe people dispersed; 'He spreads for you' means He spreads your provision.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r1.anchor: والنشر: ضد الطي، وجاء القوم نشرا: متفرقين، و(ينشر لكم ربكم) أي: ينشر رزقكم

JISHUMI:v9p6247/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r2.speaker: عائشة
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r2.claim: In a report describing Abū Bakr, ʿĀʾisha says he restored the dispersed and broken unity of Islam to its former state after the ridda.
JISHUMI:v9p6247/r2.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة تصف أباها: فرد نشر الإسلام على غره؛ أي: على طيه وكسره

JISHUMI:v9p6255/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r3.claim: God's spreading of mercy shows its breadth and His complete power: He prepares what benefits each person in each land through subtle providence.
JISHUMI:v9p6255/r3.anchor: على عموم رحمته وكمال قدرته، حيث هيأ لكل أحد ما يصلحه في كل بلد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r2.claim: When told land was parched and people despaired, Umar replied that they would then receive rain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r2.anchor: قيل لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه : جدبت الأرض وقنط الناس فقال : مطروا إذن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r3.claim: Ghayth is beneficial rain in its proper season; matar may be harmful or beneficial and arrive in or out of season.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r3.anchor: والغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته , والمطر قد يكون ضارا ونافعا في وقته وغير وقته .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r4.claim: God spreads His mercy through rain, in ways that are general and particular.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r4.anchor: وينشر رحمته } بالغيث فيما يعم ويخص .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r5.claim: One reading takes al-Wali as owner and al-Hamid as deserving praise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r5.anchor: أحدهما : الولي المالك , والحميد مستحق الحمد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p203/r6.claim: Another reading takes al-Wali as benefactor and al-Hamid as praised.

MUJAHID:v2p575#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p575#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p575#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses their despair as having given up hope.
MUJAHID:v2p575#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا ﴾ يقول من بعد ما يئسوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r1.claim: The verb is read with a doubled zāy by Medinans, Syrians and ʿĀṣim; another reading is reported for qanitu.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r1.anchor: بالتشديد مدنى وشامى وعاصم ﴿ من بعد ما قنطوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r2.claim: Spreading mercy means the rain's blessings, benefits and fertility; another possibility is Allah's mercy in all things.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r2.anchor: اى بركات الغيث ومنافعه وما يحصل به من الخصب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r3.speaker: عمر
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r3.claim: When told that drought had become severe and people despaired, ʿUmar reportedly said, “They have been rained upon,” apparently invoking this verse or its promise of mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r3.anchor: وقيل لعمر رضى الله عنه اشتد القحط وقنط الناس فقال مطروا اذا اراد هذه الاية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r4.claim: Al-Walī is the one who cares for His servants through beneficence; al-Ḥamīd is praised for it by those who obey Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p103#2/r4.anchor: الذى يتولى عباده باحسانه ﴿ الحميد ﴾ المحمود على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن محيصن، حميد، مجاهد، أبو عمرو، يعقوب، ابن وثاب، الأعمش، الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r1.claim: These readers pronounce yunazzilu without gemination; the remaining readers use the doubled form.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد ومجاهد وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن وثاب والأعمش وغيرهما والكسائي «ينزل» مخففا

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r2.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r2.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the verb with gemination.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r2.anchor: الباقون بالتشديد. وقرأ ابن وثاب أيضا والأعمش وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r3.speaker: ابن وثاب، الأعمش
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r3.claim: Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, and others also read qanatū with kasra on the nūn.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب أيضا والأعمش وغيرهما «قنطوا» بكسر النون

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r4.claim: Al-ghayth means rain and is so named because it comes to the aid of creatures; the verb also describes rain reaching land or God giving rain to a country.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r4.anchor: والغيث المطر وسمي الغيث غيثا لأنه يغيث الخلق. وقد غاث الغيث الأرض أي أصابها

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī recounts an Arab woman answering that they were rained upon as much as they wished; al-Thaʿlabī transmits this first anecdote.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r5.anchor: وعن الأصمعي قال: مررت ببعض قبائل العرب وقد مطروا فسألت عجوزا منهم: أتاكم المطر؟ فقالت: غثنا ما شئنا غيثا

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r6.speaker: ذو الرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r6.claim: Dhu al-Rumma praises a woman’s eloquent use of “ghithnā”; al-Jawharī transmits this second anecdote.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r6.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة: قاتل الله أمة بني فلان ما أفصحها قلت لها كيف كان المطر عندكم؟ فقالت: غثنا ما شئنا

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r7.claim: Clouds and vegetation may also be called ghayth.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r8.claim: Qunūṭ means despair, as Qatāda and others explain.

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r9.claim: Qatāda reports that a man told ʿUmar people despaired amid drought; ʿUmar replied that rain would come, God willing, and recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب: يا أمير المؤمنين، قحط المطر وقل الغيث

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r10.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r10.claim: Al-Māwardī distinguishes ghayth, beneficial rain in its proper season, from rain, which can benefit or harm in season or out of season.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r10.anchor: والغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته، والمطر قد يكون نافعا وضارا في وقته وغير وقته قاله الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r11.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r11.claim: Al-Suddī interprets God’s spreading mercy as the rain itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r11.anchor: { وينشر رحمته } قيل المطر وهو قول السدي

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r12.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r12.claim: Al-Mahdawī gives another interpretation: the sun appearing after rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r12.anchor: وقيل ظهور الشمس بعد المطر ذكره المهدوي

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r13.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r13.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed after rain was withheld from Mecca’s people for seven years, until they despaired and God sent rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في حبس المطر عن أهل مكة سبع سنين حتى قنطوا، ثم أنزل الله المطر

QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r14.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:42:28/r14.claim: Al-Qushayrī offers the occasion of a Bedouin asking the Prophet about rain on Friday, in the report of the rain prayer.
